name: Sunvoy
headline: Sunvoy unified API for solar hardware and financing data
summary: Sunvoy tackles the N+1 integration problem: one RESTful API that normalizes telemetry from 30+ inverter brands (including Enphase and SolarEdge), batteries, and financing platforms such as GoodLeap, Mosaic, Sunlight Financial, and Dividend.

key_facts.label: Pattern
key_facts.value: Single unified REST API across hardware + finance vendors

sections.heading: Post-install telemetry meets loan tracking
sections.body: Unlike proposal-only aggregators, Sunvoy emphasizes ongoing operations: inverter production, storage behavior, and financing status in one normalized feed. Asset managers and software teams can monitor performance and payment state without maintaining separate OAuth flows per vendor.

sections.heading: Solving N+1 integrations
sections.body: Without a unifier, each manufacturer and lender means another key rotation policy, schema, and failure mode. Sunvoy collapses that to one integration surface with a predictable response format — useful for portfolios, not just single-home sales tools.

sections.heading: Usage-based cost control
sections.body: Most calls cost one credit (on the order of a fraction of a cent). That granularity helps developers prototype affordably and scale deliberately — though production architectures should still cache where freshness allows.

sections.heading: Homeowner relevance
sections.body: You may never log into Sunvoy. You will feel it if your installer’s monitoring app or financier portal shows production and loan milestones in one place. If monitoring and loan servicing feel disconnected, ask who aggregates your hardware data and who services the note.

questions_to_ask: Which monitoring platform will I use after PTO, and does it include financing status?
If my inverter brand changes mid-project, does monitoring still work?
Who do I call for loan servicing vs production issues?
red_flags: No monitoring plan disclosed before deposit.
Financing and production support contacts that bounce you between vendors indefinitely.

faqs.question: Is Sunvoy a solar lender?
faqs.answer: No. It is a unified API layer over hardware telemetry and financing platforms.

faqs.question: Does SolarFlow use Sunvoy?
faqs.answer: SolarFlow models ROI and roof layouts for homeowners; this page explains an industry aggregator you may encounter indirectly through installer/ops software.
